# Who can actually decide?

Move local information, decision authority and consequences among two fictional teams and a coordination desk. Compare local, central and informed local arrangements under the same requests. Separate outcomes show local fit, cross-team compatibility, queue timing and who carries adverse effects.

The pure engine uses finite role slots and one arrival-ordered queue for decisions and permissions. Accurate consultation adds a fixed delay; permission adds no facts. Edit workload, coupling, methods, timing and capacities. All requests arrive together; no learning, negotiation or empirical staffing forecast is implied.

`model.test.js` exercises queue capacity, information timing, independent-demand and common-needs counterexamples, consequence assignment and matched comparisons. The native app and article definition use the same engine and queue figure.

Inspired by [John Cutler, Exception, Presence, Delegation](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-422-exception-presence-delegation).
